question: $\overrightarrow{OA} = \mathbf{a}$ and $\overrightarrow{OB} = \mathbf{b}$.
$C$ lies on $AB$ with $AC : CB = 3 : 1$.
Find $\overrightarrow{OC}$ in terms of $\mathbf{a}$ and $\mathbf{b}$.

wrong.why: the 3 sits next to A, so it feels right

trap: C is close to B, so it needs more b.

beats.say: Most students get this wrong. C lies on A B, with A C to C B equal to three to one. Find vector O C, in terms of vectors A and B.
Pause. What do you think the next step is?
Many write three quarters of vector A, plus one quarter of vector B. The three sits next to A in the ratio, so it feels right.
But C is three quarters of the way from A to B. It sits close to B, so it needs more of vector B, not less.
Start at A, then go three quarters of the way along A B. And A B is the vector B minus A.
Expand and collect. O C is one quarter of vector A, plus three quarters of vector B.

verify:
a, b = symbols('a b')
C = a + Rational(3, 4) * (b - a)
assert expand(C - (a / 4 + 3 * b / 4)) == 0
# AC : CB = 3 : 1
assert expand((C - a) - 3 * (b - C)) == 0
wrong = 3 * a / 4 + b / 4
assert expand(wrong - C) != 0

youtube.description: C lies on AB with AC : CB = 3 : 1. Is OC = ¾a + ¼b? No — C sits close to B, so it needs more b. OC = ¼a + ¾b.
